intent_en: To demonstrate that national polling accuracy for presidential elections has improved significantly over time, with recent polls being much more accurate than in the past.
previous_intent: To illustrate the increasing accuracy of national presidential polls over time, showing a reduction in average error from 1936 to 2016.
narration_support: national polling in presidential elections is more accurate now than it was a few decades ago.
chart_support: Line chart showing the average error in final national presidential polls from 1936 to 2016, with an inverted y-axis (Less accurate at top, More accurate at bottom) displaying a general downward trend in error (upward trend in accuracy).
evidence_note: The narration explicitly claims increased accuracy, and the chart visualizes this by plotting average error decreasing from 1936 to 2016, with specific callouts showing high error in the past and low error recently.
